1 Introduction                                                        To support AVM, kernels have to be written dif-
    Virtual memory is an important, hard-to-                     ferently: instead of abstracting physical memory and
implement, and performance-critical operating system             TLBs, kernels should safely export and multiplex VM
abstraction. Many operating systems implement this               resources directly to application level. We call such a
abstraction completely in the kernel. These systems              kernel an exokernel [9, 10] (to be precise, exokernels
are typically large, complex, and in flexible, resulting           strive to export all resources, not just those necessary
in bad performance and poor reliability.                         to support AVM). The AVM system we describe in this
    To allow some degree of customization and to sim-            paper is built on top of our prototype exokernel, Aegis.
